milestone: M12-E send-outcome uncertainty, one-shot submission, and local hash tracking
git_commit_reading: read .git/HEAD (ref: refs/heads/main), then the loose ref it names
how_this_file_was_built: every figure below is read out of a gate log, a committed evidence file, the worktree diff, or a source file by /tmp/m12e_manifest.py; no figure is typed in by hand

standing_verdicts.how_known: the only socket in this round's measurement is a `std::net::TcpListener` bound to 127.0.0.1:0 inside the test process; production code was not run against any network, and the two verification transactions of M7 remain the only real submissions in this repository's history
standing_verdicts.process_restart_persistence: UNSOLVED — M12-D §13.2 stays open. The local hash this round tracks is a field of an in-process enum; nothing writes it down, so a restart forgets it

scope.how_measured: production and test diffs from `git diff --numstat`; new-file line counts and `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attributes counted from the files themselves

commands: cargo clean -p <each of the 16 workspace packages>
gates.why_no_fail_fast: gate 3 runs with --no-fail-fast so a red target cannot hide the rest of the workspace behind it; --test-threads=1 is the repository's standing rule because target/pipeline-tests/ scratch is shared across processes

cold_run.why: a warm clippy re-analyses nothing, so the exposure of the gate could not be stated from its own log; every workspace package was cleaned first and dependencies were left cached

test.ignored_is_not_passed: the ignored names below are counted in `ignored` only, never in `passed`

audit_9.question: all production `eth_sendRawTransaction` call sites
audit_9.answer: 1 production line passes the method to the transport; 1 further mention sits behind a `#[cfg(test)]` module in a src file
audit_9.how_measured: walk of every non-test .rs file under crates/, comment lines dropped, each hit placed before or after that file's `#[cfg(test)]` line

audit_9.question: a bypass of the one-shot path
audit_9.answer: none: the only submission site calls `request_raw_once`, asserted by `the_send_path_anchors_resolve_and_no_submission_takes_the_retrying_entry`
audit_9.how_measured: the same walk, plus the gate's per-site `request_raw_once` assertion

audit_9.question: a submission still on the generic retry loop
audit_9.answer: none: `WirePolicy::Once` allows one attempt and `request_with` passes `RetryOnce` only through `request`/`request_raw`, which no send path uses
audit_9.how_measured: the attempt counts are read out of `WirePolicy::attempts` by the evidence gate, and every answered send row in the table carries send_arrivals equal to that figure

audit_9.question: a path that turns `Unknown` into `Rejected`, `Accepted`, or an empty opportunity
audit_9.answer: none in production: the lifecycle matches the variant and holds the lane for `Unknown`; only `Rejected` reaches a failure path that releases it
audit_9.how_measured: `proven_not_in_flight` is the only release gate, and the rows carry both the outcome word and the release word

audit_9.question: a lane released on a hash mismatch
audit_9.answer: impossible by construction: a mismatched or absent hash builds `Unknown`, and release is gated on `proven_not_in_flight()`, which is `Rejected` alone
audit_9.how_measured: `never_absolved`, `lane_release_word` and `classifier_recomputed` rules over the measured rows, and the two hash-mismatch cases in the matrix

audit_9.question: errors or trace leaking an endpoint URL, API key or JWT
audit_9.answer: no row in the measurement carries any of the eleven needles, and every socket is named by an `rpc-<16 hex>` digest
audit_9.how_measured: `no_endpoint_leak` over all rows; the two §9 item 6 cases inject a URL into the transport's own message and re-read it out

audit_9.question: trace attempt count against real HTTP requests
audit_9.answer: one trace attempt per socket arrival, and zero dropped events
audit_9.how_measured: `trace_matches_socket` over the §9 item 7 row, which carries both the stub's tally and the trace's own counts

audit_9.question: new code introducing RPC calls
audit_9.how_measured: `git diff -U0 -- '*/src/*'`, added and removed lines scanned for `eth_` string literals; only the send method appears, and it already existed

audit_9.question: a test or build touching historical evidence
audit_9.answer: see cross_milestone_anchor_refresh and known_staleness below: the M10 manifest was re-stamped by a gate and restored, and the ten M8 tables differ only in anchor line numbers, which the next section checks structurally rather than asserts
audit_9.how_measured: `git status --porcelain` before and after the gate run, then a leaf-by-leaf JSON diff of each changed historical file against HEAD

definite_messages_from_production: max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas

evidence.measurement_command: M12E_EVIDENCE_DIR=<absolute path to data/evidence/m12/e> cargo test -p evm-execution --test send_uncertainty -- --test-threads=1
evidence.what_the_evidence_is_not: a local HTTP stub on loopback, not a GIWA node; no transaction entered a block; `submitted` is not `Mined`, `Confirmed` or realized profit; the local hash a row tracks lives in the process that wrote it

cross_milestone_anchor_refresh.why_this_is_in_scope: this milestone moved lines in crates/chain/src/rpc.rs and crates/execution/src/giwa/sequencer_direct.rs; those gates re-resolve `file`+`token` anchors from that source, so their displayed line numbers moved

known_staleness.what_changed: its `git_commit` is reprinted by crates/execution/tests/executor_evidence_gate.rs on any workspace test run
known_staleness.handling: restored to the committed bytes before the evidence commit; the behaviour itself is left as an out-of-scope finding rather than patched in this round

known_staleness.what_changed: nothing — its `public_http_rpc` class word on the submission side is superseded by M12-E §5's `over endpoint <digest>`, which the production code now emits
known_staleness.why_not_edited: historical evidence is not rewritten by a later milestone

known_staleness.artifact: test fixtures that construct `SubmissionOutcome::Rejected { reason: "nonce too low" }`
known_staleness.why_recorded: §4 says a pool answer is not a definite refusal. These are hand-built variants that never pass through the classifier, so they do not contradict the production path — but they are a poor model for a future test, and the report names them instead of editing them here

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: cross-process persistence of an uncertain send
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: the local hash, the lane hold and the tracking state all live in the process that sent the transaction. A restart before the receipt side resolves the outcome forgets the transaction entirely, and the next run can allocate the same nonce and re-send.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: M12-E §8 forbids a persistent execution ledger, and §6 forbids a second state machine or reconciliation service. M12-D §13.2 names this gap already.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: a ledger task that stores the unresolved send and re-adopts it on boot

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: the receipt side has no bound on how long it holds a lane after `Unknown`
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: `Unknown` holds the nonce lane and the receipt tracker keeps asking, with no deadline and no escalation to the operator. An unresolved send holds a lane for the life of the process.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: §6 asks only that the lane not be released as if the send had failed; a policy for when to stop waiting is a new decision, not a fix.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: pair with the persistence finding: an expiry or an explicit operator hand-off

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: a hash mismatch is carried only inside a reason string
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: when the node returns a hash that is not the local one, the outcome is `Unknown` whose reason text names both hashes. Nothing downstream can branch on `mismatch` as a machine value without parsing that string.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: §5 says to adjust `SubmissionOutcome` fields only for actual consumers, and no consumer needed the flag this round.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: add a typed field when a consumer exists, not before

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: `without_the_endpoint` scrubs exact URL strings, not a prefix tree
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: it replaces the endpoint URL and the URL with a trailing slash by the digest. An error that splits the URL across words, or reports a different path on the same host, would keep part of it.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: the eleven needles over every measured row come back clean, and the transport's own messages quote the URL whole.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: a host-level scrub if an upstream error is ever observed leaking a path

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: endpoint digests depend on the port, so they are not joinable across milestones
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: `evm_chain::endpoint_id(url)` hashes the URL as given. The same host on an ephemeral stub port yields a different digest in every run, so digests are only comparable inside one measurement.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: the evidence here never compares a digest across runs; it only checks shape and uniqueness inside one table.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: only matters if a later milestone wants a cross-run endpoint census

out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.finding: `executor_evidence_gate` re-stamps its own manifest on every workspace run
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.detail: the gate writes `git_commit` into data/evidence/m10/manifest.json, so any `cargo test --workspace` leaves the historical evidence file dirty.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_here: M10's own gate design; changing it edits a historical milestone's behaviour, which §8 forbids. This round restores the committed bytes instead.
out_of_scope_findings_recorded_not_fixed.suggested_task: make that gate compare in memory rather than write, in a maintenance task
